stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and null spec. Live preview across GO, UP, and MX platforms is a complex real-time feature requiring full requirement elaboration and hardening. Openspec runs first to draft ACs and add technical depth; speckit follows to add testability, security checks, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a novel capability: Live Preview of Content in CMS. No existing preview mechanism found in the indexed codebase. The central attachment point is useContent, which is the single content-fetching hook used by all 236 Contentstack component callers. Live Preview SDK integration must plug into this layer. Acceptance criteria are empty and description is a one-liner, so VCs are derived solely from the description intent.

Openspec provided empty AC with a valuable architectural note identifying useContent as the central integration point (236 callers). I created all 13 ACs from scratch based on the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS', the three-site scope, and the file paths (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx). Key design decisions: AC-1 covers the core happy path; AC-2 ensures zero-regression fallback when preview is not configured; AC-3/AC-13 handle error/resilience scenarios (connection loss, SDK init failure); AC-4 prevents memory leaks on unmount; AC-5 addresses rapid-edit debouncing/convergence; AC-6 enforces production safety; AC-7 provides an observable preview indicator; AC-8 explicitly guards the 236 existing callers; AC-9 enforces cross-site parity; AC-10/AC-11 handle edge cases for unsupported content types and UID mismatches; AC-12 addresses rendering efficiency. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, etc. The hook signature, existing error-handling patterns, and Contentstack SDK version would refine AC-8 (return shape compatibility) and AC-11 (UID comparison mechanism). A human should verify these ACs against the actual code.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the critical architectural integration point (useContent hook, 236 callers) and confirmed no existing preview mechanism exists, while speckit produced 13 comprehensive ACs from scratch covering happy path, fallback, error handling, memory leaks, debouncing, production safety, cross-site parity, and edge cases. However, the pipeline did not function as designed: openspec was expected to draft initial ACs for speckit to harden, but it only provided an architectural note (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0). Speckit then had to create all ACs without the benefit of openspec's elaboration step, and explicitly flagged that it could not read the actual source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx). This means AC-8 (return shape compatibility for 236 callers) and AC-11 (UID comparison mechanism) are based on assumptions about code that was never inspected. A human should verify all 13 ACs against the real source code before implementation begins.
